turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr Iyer, in you come. Headache again, or has it changed?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It has changed, doctor, and I'm honestly frightened. The old headache is there for years, but morning time it feels different.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many years?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Eight years. I was thirty-four, I'm forty-two now. Well, actually, seven or eight, somewhere there.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, Meena, his wife. He will soften it. Three weeks now he wakes holding his head, almost every morning.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Not almost every morning. Three weeks, yes, but some mornings are okay. Don't stretch it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Twice this week, early morning. The headache starts, I feel sick, then I bring up.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I checked, it's normal.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blurred vision? Double vision?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing with the eyes. I keep testing myself because my mind runs.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weakness of the arms or legs?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. I don't think so, no.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which tablets?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan, the migraine one. I nearly said hundred mg, sorry, it's fifty mg, when the pain comes. And Crocin, quite a lot.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Crocin — strength, and how often?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Five hundred mg. Most days one or two, sometimes three if the head is really bad.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sumatriptan, times in a week?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe four or five. I don't keep a count. If I skip it I'm scared the pain will shoot up.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He snores also, doctor, whole night, very loud. Afternoon he is tired and nods off on the sofa.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not snore, she is exaggerating. And I am not tired — I sleep late only because of office work.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Neck pain? Pain on bending?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neck is alright.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Please tell me straight, is this a tumour? My cousin had some brain problem and I have not slept properly thinking of it.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Can't call it a tumour from this. Fits? Blackouts?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No fits, no blackouts.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Years back the clinic near the house said migraine. That is why they started the sumatriptan.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablet? BP, sugar?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Only Crocin and the sumatriptan. Nothing else.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): If there is pressure will they operate? We have a small child, I can't just disappear for surgery.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Look at my finger. Pupils are equal and reacting. No neck stiffness.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Squeeze my fingers. Power is full in both arms and both legs. Reflexes are normal, and your gait is steady.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): BP is one thirty-two over eighty-four. Pulse seventy-six.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Is one thirty-two high for me? My father had BP. Do I need a tablet for that also?
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. BP is fine. This is your old migraine with a change in pattern, morning pain plus vomiting. I can't rule out a pressure problem inside.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): So it might be serious? Which test, and can we do it today? I don't want to wait if it's dangerous.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the morning vomiting is still there after two weeks, we'll book a CT of the head.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Is CT radiation very much? Can that itself cause a problem? What if waiting two weeks is wrong?

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): One CT, if we need it, is reasonable. Come back in two weeks either way. Cut the Crocin to not more than two a day and not on most days, and sumatriptan to not more than two days in a week.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): If I skip Crocin the pain just sits. At least one at night is okay?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): One at night is fine if you need it. Don't take three.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): What about his snoring? Should we do a sleep study?
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not now. He doesn't accept the snoring. We'll see at review.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): So you are not saying there is a growth, yes? The word pressure is scaring me.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not a firm diagnosis. Working impression only. If vomiting keeps coming, or weakness or vision change starts, don't wait out the two weeks.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I take three cups of filter coffee. Is that causing all this? Should I stop it fully?
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can't say it's the cause. Keep it to one cup till review.
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will bring him. Left to himself he will postpone.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two weeks, this OPD. If the vomiting has settled and the mornings are easier, we can skip the CT. If you worsen, come sooner.
